name: Making models smaller and faster without losing power
gist: These papers compress large models and make them run quicker by removing unnecessary parts, using distillation and quantization, so they work on regular computers and phones.
explain: The most capable language models today are enormous—they have billions or even trillions of parameters, which means they require expensive GPUs to run and can only work on servers, not on your phone or laptop. But many tasks do not need the full power of a giant model. Papers in this area tackle the question of how to take a large, smart model and compress it into something smaller that still works well. The main techniques are quantization, which means storing numbers with less precision so they use less memory, and distillation, which means teaching a small model to imitate the behavior of a large one. The small model learns from the large model's outputs and becomes an approximation of it.

The tricky part is that smaller is not always simpler—a model that is too small will fail at tasks the original handled easily, which means you lose capability. Researchers have to figure out which parameters matter most and which can be removed or simplified without hurting performance. They also face a speed versus accuracy tradeoff: aggressively quantizing a model makes it fast but inaccurate because you throw away information, while keeping it more precise takes more time to run because there is more data to process. Some papers study how to quantize strategically so different parts of the model are compressed differently based on how sensitive they are, which means some parts lose more precision than others because they matter less.

The payoff is huge: a small, fast model can run on a phone and give answers in milliseconds instead of seconds, which means users get instant feedback. This opens up use cases that were impossible before, like offline assistants (no internet needed), real-time translation on mobile devices, or local processing that does not need to send data to the cloud, which protects privacy. As phones and edge devices get faster, finding the right tradeoff between model size and quality becomes increasingly important for making AI accessible, because edge devices are where most people will interact with AI.

papers.title: Positive–Unlabeled Reinforcement Learning Distillation for On-Premise Small Models

papers.title: Privileged Information Distillation for Language Models

papers.title: ProactiveLLM: Learning Active Interaction for Streaming Large Language Models

papers.title: RaGEP: Rank-aware Geometric Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on zero-shot tasks while reducing model size and inference cost across different scales.

papers.title: RefineStat: Efficient Exploration for Probabilistic Program Synthesis

papers.contribution: Achieves 33.9% average accuracy with GlobalRegret and 32.2% with LocalRegret on nine tasks (vs baseline 30.2%), with 18.1 percentage point improvement on BoolQ.

papers.title: RepSpec: Structural Re-parameterized Draft Model Training for Speculative Decoding
papers.contribution: Significantly improves accepted sequence length in speculative decoding over EAGLE while maintaining inference efficiency without adding inference cost.

papers.title: Retrieval-Aware Distillation for Transformer-SSM Hybrids

papers.title: Routing Manifold Alignment Improves Generalization of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

papers.title: SCOUT: Active Information Foraging for Long-Text Understanding with Decoupled Epistemic States

papers.title: STAR: Similarity-guided Teacher-Assisted Refinement for Super-Tiny Function Calling Models
papers.contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art performance in size classes; a 0.6B STAR model achieves best performance among all open models under certain settings.

papers.title: Stable-LoRA: Stabilizing Feature Learning of Low-Rank Adaption

papers.title: TMS: Trajectory-Mixed Supervision for On-Policy Self Distillation

papers.contribution: Enables scalable, communication-efficient federated fine-tuning with state-of-the-art FedLoRA performance across text, image, and speech modalities.

papers.contribution: Reduces rejection rates by 0.10–0.22 and delivers 10–20% speedups over strong SD baselines while achieving 2.5–3× acceleration over non-drafting decoding.

papers.contribution: Consistently stabilizes rank-1 training and matches or outperforms rank-8 baselines across multiple vision-language tasks.

papers.contribution: Achieves up to 10× speedup over vanilla LLaDA/Dream and 5× speedup over AR models without significant accuracy drop.
